## **R Package Updates October 2026**

```{r}
update.packages(ask = FALSE)
```

## **1. {gt} 1.4.0 — Export Your R Tables to PowerPoint**

**Error in \`gtsave()\`:**
! The file extension supplied (\`.pptx\`) cannot be used.
ℹ We can use:
• \`.html\`, \`.htm\` (HTML file)
• \`.png\` (PNG file)
• \`.pdf\` (PDF file)
• \`.tex\`, \`.rnw\` (LaTeX file)
• \`.rtf\` (RTF file)
• \`.docx\` (Word file)

```{r}

library(gt)

head(mtcars) |>
  gt() |>
  gtsave("cars_table.png")
```

## **2. {coresynth} 1.0.1 — A Nice Update for Causal Inference**

[CRAN](https://cran.r-project.org/package=coresynth) \| [What’s new](https://yo5uke.com/coresynth/news/index.html)

This one is probably more interesting for people working with economics, public policy, or applied research.

Let’s say you want to evaluate whether a government policy actually worked.

You have data for several regions, one of them introduced a new policy, and you want to understand what would have happened without it.

The problem, of course, is that we cannot observe both scenarios.

That’s where methods such as Synthetic Control and Synthetic Difference-in-Differences come in.

I find **{coresynth}** interesting because it brings several of these approaches together in one package.

Among others, it supports:

- Synthetic Control

- Synthetic Difference-in-Differences

- Generalized Synthetic Control

- Matrix Completion

- Time-Aware Synthetic Control

The October 1.0.1 releases brought some substantial changes, including improvements to inference and performance.

According to the developers’ benchmarks, some Synthetic Difference-in-Differences calculations became around **6 times faster**, while a particular Time-Aware Synthetic Control fit was about **10 times faster**.

Of course, these are specific benchmarks, not something we should expect for every dataset.

What I particularly like is that different methods can be accessed through a similar interface.

For example, assuming we already have a suitable panel dataset:

```{r}
# Region 1 receives treatment from 2016
panel_data$treated <- as.integer(
  panel_data$region == 1 &
    panel_data$year >= 2016
)

# Simulate outcomes with a treatment effect
panel_data$y <-
  10 + panel_data$region +
  0.2 * (panel_data$year - 2000) +
  rnorm(nrow(panel_data), sd = 0.5) +
  2 * panel_data$treated

# Estimate Synthetic Difference-in-Differences
fit <- scm_fit(
  y ~ treated | region + year,
  data = panel_data,
  method = "sdid"
)

summary(fit)
```

## simulated monthly KPI data

```{r}
set.seed(42)

data_seq <- seq(as.Date("2023-01-01"), Sys.Date(), by = "month")
n <- length(data_seq)

kpi_raw <- data_frame(
  date = data_seq,
  revenue = round(runif(n, 80000, 150000), 0),
  conversion = round(runif(n, 0.02, 0.08), 4),
  csat = round(runif(n, 0.01, 0.06), 4)
)

```

## Rolling windows: last 30 / 60 / 90 days

```{r}
today <- Sys.Date()

window_30 <- kpi_raw |> filter(date >= today - 30)
window_60 <- kpi_raw |> filter(date >= today - 60)
window_90 <- kpi_raw |> filter(date >= today - 90)
```

## Summarize each window

```{r}
summarize_kpis <- function(df) {
  df |>  summarise(
    revenue = mean(revenue, na.rm = TRUE),
    conversion = mean(conversion, na.rm = TRUE),
    csat = mean(csat, na.rm = TRUE),
    churn = mean(churn, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
}

scorecard <- bind_rows(
  summarize_kpis(window_30 |> mutate(window = "30-Day")),
  summarize_kpis(window_60 |> mutate(window = "60-Day")),
  summarize_kpis(window_90 |> mutate(window = "90-Day"))
) |> select(window, everything())
```
